help.gameModes.title: Game Modes
help.gameModes.intro: The host picks one of two rule sets in the lobby. They differ in exactly one thing: what happens after a Tutto.
help.gameModes.modernized: The app's house rules. A completed card ends your turn immediately and banks the points. Feuerwerk lets you choose which scoring dice to keep, and Kniffel must be built as a consecutive run from 1 upward or 6 downward.
help.gameModes.classic: The official Abacusspiele rules. After any Tutto you may reveal the next card and keep going — the points accumulate, but a bust or a drawn Stop card forfeits the WHOLE turn. Feuerwerk keeps every scoring die automatically, and any still-missing number counts toward Kniffel.
help.gameModes.stats: Each rule set keeps its own statistics, records and win streaks — see the Statistics section.
help.general.step5DescClassic: If you successfully keep all 6 dice, you achieve a "Tutto" and complete the card. You then choose: bank your accumulated points, or reveal the next card and roll all six dice again. There is no limit — but a bust or a drawn Stop card loses everything from the turn.
help.general.title: General Rules
help.general.intro: Tutto is a thrilling push-your-luck card and dice game. The objective is to score points by rolling combinations, with the goal of reaching the target Winning Score (default: 6,000) and being the sole leader when the round ends — the round is always played to the end, and a tie plays on.
help.general.step1Desc: At the start of your turn, draw exactly one card from the deck. This card determines the special rules, bonuses, or restrictions for your turn.
help.general.step3Desc: You must keep at least one valid scoring die or combination (single 1s, 5s, or triplets) from every roll. Kept dice are locked for the rest of the turn.
help.general.step4aDesc: Secure your accumulated turn points and end your turn. You can do this on most cards (Bonus, x2) after any valid roll. You cannot stop voluntarily on Feuerwerk, Kniffel, Plus/Minus, or Kleeblatt.
help.general.step4bDesc: Roll the remaining dice. However, if any roll produces *no* scoring dice, you Bust and lose all points accumulated during this turn (unless it is a Feuerwerk card).
help.general.step5Desc: If you successfully keep all 6 dice, you achieve a "Tutto" and complete the card. Your turn then stops immediately, the card's bonus is applied, and you score your points. You do not draw another card during your turn.
help.cards.title: Cards
help.cards.bonusDesc: Achieve a Tutto (keep all 6 dice) to receive the extra points (200, 300, 400, 500, or 600 points) shown on the card. You may choose to Stop & Score at any time before finishing to keep your current turn points. Your turn ends immediately after achieving the Tutto. If you bust before achieving a Tutto, the bonus points are not awarded, and you score 0 points for the turn.
help.cards.bonusDescClassic: Achieve a Tutto (keep all 6 dice) to receive the extra points (200, 300, 400, 500, or 600 points) shown on the card. You may choose to Stop & Score at any time before finishing to keep your current turn points. After the Tutto you choose: bank everything, or reveal the next card and keep going. If you bust before achieving a Tutto, the whole turn is forfeited.
help.cards.x2Desc: Completing a Tutto doubles all points accumulated during this entire turn. You may choose to Stop & Score at any time before finishing to keep your current turn points (undoubled). Your turn ends immediately after achieving the Tutto. If you bust before achieving a Tutto, you score 0 points.
help.cards.x2DescClassic: Completing a Tutto doubles your ENTIRE accumulated turn total — including everything earned on earlier cards in the chain. You may Stop & Score before finishing to keep the current total undoubled. After the doubling Tutto you may bank or keep chaining.
help.cards.stopDesc: A bad draw! Your turn ends immediately. You score 0 points for this turn, and play passes to the next player.
help.cards.fireworksDesc: You must roll. After each roll you choose which scoring dice to keep — at least one. **You cannot stop voluntarily** and must continue rolling as long as you do not bust. If you achieve a Tutto (keep all 6 dice), you score the points and must continue rolling with all 6 dice again. Your turn only ends when you Bust, but you **keep all points** accumulated during this Feuerwerk turn.
help.cards.fireworksDescClassic: You must roll. **All scoring dice are automatically kept** for you after each roll (the official rule). **You cannot stop voluntarily** and must continue rolling as long as you do not bust. If you achieve a Tutto, you continue rolling all 6 dice on this same card. The null that ends the Feuerwerk **banks your entire accumulated turn** — even the points from earlier cards in a chain.
help.cards.kniffelDesc: You must roll a straight (1-2-3-4-5-6) in sequence. On the first roll, you must keep either a 1 or a 6. For subsequent rolls, you must keep the next consecutive number (ascending if you started with 1, descending if you started with 6). A roll containing several numbers in a row lets you keep the whole run at once. **You cannot stop voluntarily** and must continue rolling until you complete the straight or bust. Completing the straight (Tutto) awards exactly 2,000 points, and your turn ends. Busting awards 0 points.
help.cards.kniffelDescClassic: You must collect all six numbers (1-6), **in any order** — every die showing a number you have not yet put aside is valid, and you must keep at least one per roll. A roll without any still-missing number is a null. **You cannot stop voluntarily.** Completing the straight adds exactly 2,000 points and counts as a Tutto — you may then bank or reveal the next card.
help.cards.plusMinusDesc: You must achieve a Tutto to score. **You cannot stop voluntarily** and must continue rolling until Tutto or bust. Once Tutto is achieved, your turn ends and you score exactly 1,000 points. **Every** player tied for the lead then loses 1,000 points — all of them, not just one. If you are among the leaders yourself, nobody is deducted at all. If you Bust, you score 0.
help.cards.plusMinusDescClassic: You must achieve a Tutto — **you cannot stop voluntarily**, and the dice rolled on this card score nothing by themselves. A Tutto adds exactly **+1,000** to your turn total, and you may then bank or keep chaining. **Every** player tied for the lead loses 1,000 points (never below 0) — all of them, not just one. If you are one of several tied leaders, the others still lose theirs and you keep yours; only a player leading **alone** deducts from nobody. The deduction happens **when you bank the turn** — a later bust forfeits it along with everything else.
help.cards.kleeblattDesc: The ultimate challenge! You must achieve **two Tuttos in a row** without stopping. Roll all 6 dice and keep them all (1st Tutto), then roll all 6 dice again and keep them all (2nd Tutto). **You cannot stop voluntarily** and must continue rolling. If successful, you win the game immediately! Busting on either roll awards 0 points.
help.settings.title: Game Settings
help.settings.winningScore: Winning Score: Target points to win. Range: 1,000 to 99,999 (default: 6,000). To win, a player must reach the winning score and be the sole leader when the round ends — the round is always played to the end, and a tie plays on.
help.settings.turnTimer: Turn Timer: Limit on turn duration. Range: 10s to 600s, or 0 to disable (default: 120s). Only in online games. Feuerwerk turns get a 3x multiplier, Kleeblatt turns get a 2x multiplier.
help.settings.kickTimer: Kick Timer (Reconnect Timeout): Duration a disconnected player is allowed to rejoin before being kicked. Range: 10s to 3,600s, or 0 to disable (default: 60s). Only in online games.
help.settings.randomOrder: Random Order: Randomizes player turn order at the start.
help.settings.diceMode: Dice Mode: Choose between Digital (virtual rolling) and Physical (rolling real dice and inputting the results). The host can enforce a single mode.
help.settings.deckComp: Deck Composition: Customize the number of copies of each card type in the deck (0 to 99). The deck must contain at least one card to start.
help.online.title: Playing Online
help.online.intro: A room is just a code you pick — anyone who enters the same code joins you. Rather than reading it out, hand it over:
help.online.inviteLink: Invite link: the copy button beside the room name copies a link that opens Tutto with the code already filled in. Your guest only has to supply their name.
help.online.share: Share: on a device with a share sheet, the share button hands that same link straight to it.
help.online.qr: QR code: the QR button shows the link as a code. Whoever is sitting next to you can open it with their phone's own camera app — Tutto does not need to be involved at all.
help.online.scan: Scan: the scan button beside the room code opens the camera to read someone else's QR code, for when you already have Tutto open and would rather not leave it.
help.online.recentRooms: Recent rooms: rooms you have joined are listed under the join form so you can go back with one tap. The × beside one forgets it.
help.online.scanSecure: Scanning needs a secure (https) connection, because browsers only allow camera access on one. Everything else here works over plain http too — including a guest scanning your QR code with their own camera.
help.shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
help.shortcuts.intro: On a desktop you can play a whole turn without reaching for the mouse.
help.shortcuts.primary: Do whatever the big button does right now — roll the dice, end your turn, or answer Yes.
help.shortcuts.rollAgain: Roll again with the dice you have selected (inside the dice panel).
help.shortcuts.stop: Stop and bank the dice you have selected (inside the dice panel).
help.shortcuts.selectAll: Select every die in the current roll that scores.
help.shortcuts.drawNextCard: Draw the next card instead of banking, on the roll that completes a Tutto (Classic rules).
help.shortcuts.note: Shortcuts stay out of the way while you are typing in a field and while a dialog is open, and a key does nothing when its button is grayed out.
help.statistics.title: Statistics Explained
help.statistics.s1: Games Played / Wins / Win Rate: Track your overall game results.
help.statistics.s2: Busts / Average Busts per Game: The count and rate of rolling no scoring dice on a turn.
help.statistics.s3: Hit by −1000: The number of times you had 1,000 points deducted due to another player's Plus/Minus success.
help.statistics.s4: Highest Turn Score: The maximum points you've scored in a single turn.
help.statistics.s5: Fastest Win (turns): The minimum number of turns you took to win a game.
help.statistics.s6: Success vs Failures: Tracks outcomes for Kniffel, Plus/Minus, and Kleeblatt cards.
help.statistics.s7: Four buckets: each rule set (Modernized / Classic) keeps its own statistics, records and win streaks, and within each, only games on the default winning score and default deck count as normal — changing either records the game under that rule set's Custom bucket instead. The turn timer, kick timer, random order and an enforced dice mode make no difference. Local games are never recorded.
help.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
help.faq.a1: A Tutto occurs when all 6 dice are scoring and kept. This completes the active card and ends your turn with the card's success (or lets you roll all 6 dice again if it is a Feuerwerk card).
help.faq.a1Classic: A Tutto occurs when all 6 dice are scoring and kept. This completes the active card — you may then bank your points or reveal the next card and keep going (a Feuerwerk Tutto instead keeps rolling on the same card).
help.faq.a2: Single 1s (100 pts), single 5s (50 pts). Three-of-a-kind (triplets): Three 1s = 1000, three 2s = 200, three 3s = 300, three 4s = 400, three 5s = 500, three 6s = 600.
help.faq.a3: No, only groups of three score. The fourth die does not score (unless it's a 1 or 5).
help.faq.a4: No, you must roll at least once per card.
help.faq.q5: Can I draw another card if I finish my current card?
help.faq.a5: Not under the Modernized rules — your turn consists of exactly one card draw. Once you finish the card (achieve a Tutto) or choose to stop, your turn ends. Switch to Classic if you want to chain cards.
help.faq.a5Classic: Yes — that is the heart of Classic. After every Tutto you choose: bank the accumulated points, or reveal the next card and roll all six dice again. A bust or a drawn Stop card loses the whole turn.
help.faq.q6: How does the Undo button work?
help.faq.a6: In both local and online games, players can undo the previous turn if a mistake was made, reverting the game state. In online games, only the active player or the host can trigger the Undo.
help.faq.a7: You roll real dice on your table and enter the values into the app's prompt.
